thread:
zara (ML Eng): Quick heads-up — we saw a quality regression on long-context prompts after enabling a hybrid fp8+int4 precision profile for gpt-j-ld. Short prompts look fine, long ones hallucinate more. Anyone else hit this?

devon (Runtime): Noticed increased perplexity on the validation set too. Logs show more kv-cache evictions when sequence > 8k.

sam (Research): Can you paste the profile you used? Might be a layer boundary mismatch.

zara (ML Eng): Sure — config we rolled: 
```
precision_profile:
  - layer_range: [0, 6]
    precision: fp8
  - layer_range: [7, -1]
    precision: int4
fallback_policy: degrade_to:int8@latency>200ms
```

devon (Runtime): That looks fine on paper. But runtime is swapping int4 kernels for attention key/value writes; int4 kv packing is less robust for long sequences, I think.

lia (SRE): Timeline: we flipped canary at 03:10 UTC, ramped to 20% at 04:00, customer reports came in at ~05:30. Rollback at 06:15.

alex (Payload): Observed weird tokenization drift — outputs start fine then veer off after ~2k tokens. Could be numeric instability when mixing fp8 -> int4 mid-stack.

sam (Research): Two hypotheses: 1) quantization error propagation through attention when keys/values are in int4; 2) KV cache alignment/padding bug for packed int4 buffers.

devon (Runtime): I can add extra sanity checks: detect kv cache mismatch between steps and dump minimal repro. Will push a lightweight assert to canary.

quant-bot: Canary build deployed to cohort-42 at 3476543225; debug flags enabled.

zara (ML Eng): Thanks. Also can we validate if fp8->int4 boundary on residual branch is okay? Some architectures rely on FP accumulation on the residual path.

sam (Research): I'll run targeted evals: 1) long-context factuality suite, 2) attention-score divergence diagnostics, 3) layerwise quant error heatmap. Expect results in ~3 hours.

lia (SRE): Metric watch: latency stayed within SLO for most, but error-rate spiked (400s) on the cluster where canary ran. Might be memory alignment causing OOMs for packing.

devon (Runtime): If packing alignment is the culprit we can try force-aligning buffers at the boundary or keep KV in fp8 while weights are int4 for those layers. There's also runtime flag `--kv-no-pack-int4` I can toggle.

alex (Payload): Quick experiment idea: keep early layers fp8, middle layers int4, but force kv-cache type to fp8 across all layers to isolate packing vs quant error.

zara (ML Eng): Good - prefer that experiment before dropping low-bit strategy. If quality holds with kv forced to fp8, it's a packing bug. If it still fails, then quant error propagation.

devon (Runtime): I'll run both variants on canary with debug dumps. Plan: a) toggle --kv-no-pack-int4; b) force kv type fp8. Each run with 1000 long-context queries.

sam (Research): If we find quant error is the root, we should consider per-head or per-attn-term scaling factors rather than coarse layer-level profiles. That's a longer RFC.

lia (SRE): Logging action: keep the canary on until we have debug dumps. If OOM rate > 1% we cut immediately.

zara (ML Eng): Action items: devon add asserts + run two canary variants; sam run diagnostics and hypothesis tests; alex collate customer repros; lia monitor OOM + error rate.

alex (Payload): Collating now, will post a small repro in thread shortly.

devon (Runtime): Pushed flag and assert at 3476543248, running variant A now.

sam (Research): Kickoff evals at 3476543255.

zara (ML Eng): Thanks team. If we confirm a packing bug, runtime fix + an emergency test in our CI to run one long-context quant mix test before promotable.

devon (Runtime): Agreed. Also adding a runtime safety: block hybrid fp8->int4 profiles for models with >8k seq until validated.

zara (ML Eng): OK let's reconvene after results. :mag_right:

quant-bot: Debug traces uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/canary/3476543210/ (restricted).

alex (Payload): Posted minimal repro (prompt + expected vs actual tokens) at 3476543272.

sam (Research): Early findings: attention-score drift correlates with boundary layer index 7-9, and magnitude grows with sequence length. Preliminary leaning: quant error amplification.

devon (Runtime): Variant A (--kv-no-pack-int4) reduced OOMs but didn't fix hallucination. Variant B (force kv fp8) reduced drift noticeably.

zara (ML Eng): Sounds like mixing int4 for kv is risky. Proposal: short-term: restrict kv_type=fallback(fp8) when sequence_length>4096 for hybrid profiles. Medium-term: refine profile DSL to express kv_type independently of weight precision.

sam (Research): I'll draft a short RFC for `precision_profile.kv_type` and per-layer scaling params.

devon (Runtime): I'll prototype runtime guard and CI test.

lia (SRE): I'll annotate the incident and timeline for postmortem.

zara (ML Eng): Great. Thanks all. Follow-ups: sam RFC + PR, devon runtime guard PR, alex attach repro to the issue. We'll loop back in tomorrow sync. :white_check_mark:
